sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: DSA questions at fresher level are not LeetCode hard. They're 'can you explain why a dict lookup is faster than a list search' and 'implement a stack using a list'. Get these right and the coding round becomes manageable.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
**Big-O is about growth rate, not absolute speed:**

| Operation | list | dict | set |
|---|---|---|---|
| Access by index | O(1) | - | - |
| Search by value | O(n) | - | - |
| Lookup by key | - | O(1) | O(1) |
| Insert at end | O(1) amortized | O(1) | O(1) |
| Insert at start | O(n) | - | - |

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **Big-O** — O(1) constant, O(log n) binary search, O(n) linear scan, O(n²) nested loops. Recognize these from code structure.
- **Stack** — LIFO. Python list with `.append()` / `.pop()`. Use for undo, call stack, balanced brackets.
- **Queue** — FIFO. `collections.deque` with `.append()` / `.popleft()`. List `.pop(0)` is O(n), deque is O(1).
- **Recursion** — every recursive function needs a base case. Call stack depth is the hidden cost.
- **Hash table** — Python dict uses this. Key must be hashable. O(1) average lookup.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **'What is the time complexity of appending to a Python list?'** — O(1) amortized (occasionally O(n) for resize).
- **'Why use deque instead of list for a queue?'** — `list.pop(0)` is O(n); `deque.popleft()` is O(1).
- **'What is a base case in recursion?'** — the condition that stops the recursion. Without it: `RecursionError`.
- **'Why is dict lookup O(1)?'** — hash of the key maps directly to a bucket. No scanning.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"When I see a problem I first ask: what structure gives me the operations I need at the right complexity? If I need fast lookup by key it's a dict. If I need order it's a list. If I need FIFO it's a deque. Then I think about the outer algorithm — can I solve it in O(n) with a hash map instead of O(n²) with nested loops?"*
